projects.name: Autonomous Search & Rescue: Frontier Exploration for Quadruped Robots
projects.title: Robotics & Autonomous Systems Engineer
projects.tldr:
• Developed an autonomous exploration framework for the Unitree Go2 quadruped, targeting hazardous, unstructured Search and Rescue (SAR) environments.
  • Implemented a perception pipeline using Bayesian log-odds updates to fuse 3D LiDAR point clouds into filtered 2D occupancy grids for stable mapping.
  • Engineered a custom frontier-based exploration node that autonomously selects mission goals by balancing Euclidean distance against area coverage utility.
  • Leveraged the ROS2 Navigation2 (Nav2) stack and tuned its Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) controller to achieve smooth navigation through narrow, debris-filled corridors.
  • Bridged high-level ROS2 velocity commands with low-level Unitree API calls to enable seamless, collision-free hardware actuation.
projects.summary:
In Search and Rescue (SAR) sectors—a market projected to reach $15.7 billion by 2031—the challenge is operating in hazardous, unknown environments. Our team developed an open-source autonomous exploration framework for the Unitree Go2 quadruped, fusing complex legged mobility with real-time mapping to navigate three-dimensional obstacles common in disaster sites.

System ArchitecturePerception-to-Actuation Pipeline



Probabilistic Mapping & Awareness

We achieved real-time environment awareness by converting the local 3D LiDAR stream into an accurate 2D occupancy grid. To ensure the map was robust against sensor noise, we implemented Bayesian log-odds updates. We tuned the occupancy probabilities (0.7 for occupied, 0.1 for free) to allow for rapid detection of static obstacles while enabling the map to "forget" dynamic noise. This created a stable foundation for both the global costmap and our autonomous planner.

Managing complex TF tree transformations (Map -> Odom -> Base_Link -> LiDAR)



Autonomous Frontier Exploration

True autonomy required the robot to identify and prioritize unexplored regions. We developed an Explorer Node that scans the occupancy grid for frontiers—boundaries between known free space and unknown territory. We implemented a utility function that selects goals based on the shortest Euclidean distance. To ensure safety, we filtered out frontier candidates located too close to obstacles or in non-traversable regions, biasing the robot toward safe, open-space exploration.

Frontier cells overlaid on the costmap with the selected goal and Nav2 optimal path



Navigation & Control Interface

Once a frontier goal is set, the Nav2 stack handles path execution. We leveraged Nav2’s Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) controller, which samples thousands of candidate control sequences to optimize for path tracking and obstacle avoidance. We then developed a dedicated cmd_vel_to_go2 node to translate these standard ROS2 velocity commands into the Unitree-specific API calls required to drive the quadruped's motors, completing the perception-planning-actuation loop.

Experimental Results

We validated the system in an unknown maze environment. The robot successfully identified the corridor layout and autonomously navigated to the dead end, updating the occupancy grid in real-time as frontiers were cleared.

Exploration StartFinal Mapping Success



Full closed-loop exploration in the maze environment

Generalizing the exploration pipeline to an open indoor setting



Project Limitations

While the system performed reliably in maze and office environments, we identified several primary areas for future improvement:

  • Frame Drift: In our current setup, the map frame is locked to the odometry (odom) frame. For large-scale environments, this leads to accumulated drift, which could be mitigated by integrating a SLAM back-end for loop closure.
  • Onboard Compute Load: All processing currently runs on the Go2's internal hardware. The high computational demand for real-time 3D-to-2D projection and MPPI sampling suggests that future iterations should explore offboard edge computing to reduce latency.
  • Dynamic Sensitivity: The pipeline is optimized for static environments; if the environment changes significantly during execution, the robot may follow a previously valid but now blocked path until the next costmap update.

projects.name: Dynamic Handstand Robot: Classical vs. Learning-Based Control
projects.title: Reinforcement Learning Engineer
projects.tldr:
• Engineered a high-fidelity expert trajectory for a 7-link humanoid, bridging the gap between kinematic keyframing and physically realizable MuJoCo motion.
  • Developed a synthesis pipeline using "privileged DOFs" (root position and torso pitch) to sketch the global motion before correcting for dynamics.
  • Implemented a physics-validation loop to ensure the reference motion respected ground contact and gravity constraints.
  • Built a custom Gymnasium environment to facilitate state-tracking rewards based on the validated expert qpos and qvel data.
  • Trained a robust neural network policy using PPO, benchmarking it against brittle classical controllers and difficult-to-tune pure RL.
projects.summary:
This project benchmarked three control paradigms—Classical, Reinforcement Learning (RL), and Imitation Learning (IL)—for a dynamic handstand task on a 7-link humanoid. While my team explored classical linearization and pure RL, I took ownership of the Imitation Learning pipeline. I identified that for complex, multi-phase robotics tasks, the primary bottleneck is not the learning algorithm itself, but the synthesis of a physically consistent expert trajectory for the agent to follow.

Classical ControlPure RL7-Link Model



Phase 1: Kinematic Sketching (No Physics)

Generating a handstand trajectory is difficult due to the non-linear transition between walking and planting. I began by creating a "ghost" trajectory in a gravity-free kinematic space. By using privileged degrees of freedom—directly commanding the torso's global position and rotation—I was able to sketch the ideal sequence of walking, crouching, and swinging without the initial struggle of balancing dynamics. This allowed me to prioritize the visual timing and reachability of the motion.

Kinematic trajectory synthesis using privileged DOFs (No Physics)



Phase 2: Physics Validation & Refinement

The core engineering challenge was converting the kinematic "ghost" motion into a physically realizable trajectory. I implemented an iterative validation loop in generate_handstand.py. This involved simulating the trajectory with gravity and collisions enabled to detect ground clipping and momentum mismatches. I developed a fix_ground_clipping algorithm that adjusted the root Z-height and joint angles to ensure the hands and feet made contact correctly, resulting in a validated expert dataset ready for imitation.

Physics-corrected reference motion with gravity and ground contact



Phase 3: Learning & Policy Deployment

With the expert trajectory finalized, training the policy became a matter of robust tracking. I built a custom Gymnasium environment where the agent was rewarded for minimizing the error between its state and the expert's qpos and qvel. Using PPO, the policy learned to generate the necessary joint torques to follow the reference path. This Imitation Learning approach provided a controller that was far smoother than pure RL and much less numerically brittle than the classical controller.

projects.name: Trackr – Personal Finance App
projects.title: Founder & Product Engineer
projects.tldr:
• Designed and developed Trackr, a modern cross-platform personal finance app built with Flutter.
  • Supports budgeting, transaction management, multi-account syncing, and powerful analytics.
  • Cloud-based, privacy-conscious architecture with offline functionality and real-time sync.
  • Friendly mascot-led onboarding, intelligent features like receipt scanning, and financial goal tracking.
  • Currently being prepared for release on app stores with plans for commercial launch.
projects.summary:
Trackr is a mobile-first personal finance app that helps users master their finances through smart budgeting, advanced analytics, and seamless cloud sync. Built using Flutter and Firebase, it offers a refined, privacy-respecting alternative to traditional finance apps.

Trackr includes intelligent features like OCR receipt scanning, financial goal tracking, and a clean Material 3 UI with dark mode. Offline-first architecture ensures uninterrupted access to finances, while real-time sync keeps data consistent across devices.

The product is currently under final development for commercial release, focused on delivering delightful, secure, and intuitive financial management for individuals worldwide.

projects.name: Tesla
projects.title: Mechanical Design Engineer Intern
projects.tldr:
• Led design and development of seven thermal coolant components for CyberCab and other vehicles.
  • Managed RFQs, DFM reviews, and approved $160,000 in tooling for $1M+ annual components.
  • Optimized thermal designs using first-principles engineering, saving $100,000+ annually.
  • Directed investigations on automation, NVH, and insulation, performing eight tests and analyzing data.
projects.summary:
I had the incredible opportunity to work as a Mechanical Design Engineer in the Bay Area, USA, as part of the Thermal Team, which is known for owning one of the best-engineered vehicle thermal systems in the world.

As a key member of the thermal team, I was responsible for seven thermal coolant hose bundles spanning two future vehicles (CyberCab and Cybertruck RWD). I led various investigations, from material selection to automation design. My role involved the full iterative process of design, prototyping, and testing, gaining hands-on experience in designing for manufacturing (DFM) and automation.

One of my significant contributions was leading the RFQ (Request for Quote) process for one of the future vehicles. This included coordinating ongoing meetings with multiple suppliers to ensure the design was ready for mass production. My efforts culminated in giving the go-ahead for over $160k in tools, which helped the company save over $100k annually, all while the components were projected to cost over $1 million a year.

What stood out most during my time at Tesla was the company's unique flat organizational structure. Despite the global challenges faced by large tech companies, Tesla operates with a lean, trusting approach that places significant ownership in its employees. This allowed me to accomplish and grow in ways I never expected, and I'm incredibly grateful for the opportunity.

Applying the knowledge I gained at Monash University, including Solid Mechanics, Dynamics, Thermal, Materials, and Tolerancing, was instrumental in my day-to-day work. I also expanded my knowledge with new topics like NVH (Noise, Vibration, and Harshness) and durability, which were critical in ensuring the success of my projects.
